subject: MAP contingency: tranche-gating proposal and acceptance window request
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP contingency: tranche-gating proposal and acceptance window request

Claire —

Following our sync this morning, we reviewed the MAP timeline against the recent integration gating notes your engineering team shared. There is a measurable risk that the current go-live acceptance window (week of Sep 6) will slip due to two items: (1) longer-than-expected API contract sign-off in the test environment, and (2) delayed data-export cleanups on your side.

I attached a proposed contingency: a tranche-gating approach that preserves the overall go-live while isolating the highest-risk features into a secondary acceptance tranche. Key bullets:
- Tranche A (core inference + auth): keep current target (week of Sep 6), requires signed MAP and committed test harness by Aug 20.
- Tranche B (analytics + long-tail integrations): shift to Sep 20–27 window, gated on successful Tranche A validation and a short follow-up smoke test.
- Customer-facing acceptance window extension: optional one-week rolling extension for Tranche A if we see a hard blocker during cutover (conditional).

We think this reduces the single-point failure risk while giving Acme a clear rollback/mitigation path. Actions we need from you this week:
1) Confirm whether Acme can commit to the test-harness delivery by Aug 20.
2) Advise if procurement needs an explicit credit/penalty clause to accept a tranche-based acceptance.

Attached: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with proposed gating checklist) and a short contingency runbook.

If you prefer, we can convert the gating terms into a short addendum to the SOW and route via DocuSign.

Thanks —

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

[Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP contingency: tranche-gating proposal and acceptance window request

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the gating spreadsheet. High level: Acme is open to tranche gating as long as the acceptance criteria for Tranche A are explicit and the commercial terms for the potential extension are documented. Procurement (cc'd) will need a short SOW addendum and any credit language spelled out.

Operational note: our integration team expects to deliver the test harness on Aug 19 (one day earlier than your ask) but we have a pending data clean-up that may slip into Aug 21 depending on approvals. I know that complicates an Aug 20 hard gate.

Can you outline a fallback if data cleanup hits Aug 21? Also, what is Redwood's threshold for triggering the one-week rolling extension? We want the mechanics on paper before committing.

Claire Wong
Sr. Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Health
claire.wong@acmehealth.com

Vivek / Claire —

Procurement here. Quick list of requirements to process an addendum:
- A one-page SOW addendum that states Tranche A acceptance criteria and the exact trigger condition for a one-week rolling extension.
- If a commercial credit is being considered, we need the credit formula (percent of monthly fee, flat credit, or service-level credit).
- A clear statement of the acceptance signatory (name/title) and a turnaround SLA for the signature (we typically allow 3 business days).

Please attach a redlined SOW so we can route internally. For now we can accept a temporary carve-out: if Tranche A fails due to a data-cleanup issue attributable to Acme, Redwood should be able to schedule a one-week extension without credit; if failure is on Redwood, propose a 10% onboarding credit for Tranche A.

Regards,
Acme Procurement Team

Subject: RE: internal: MAP contingency recommendation for Acme (prep for exec brief)

Team —

Quick internal take after procurement's reply: procurement has proposed split responsibility language and requested a credit if failure is on our side (10% onboarding credit for Tranche A). That's reasonable, but we should avoid open-ended credits and tie any financial concession to two constraints:
1) Binding MAP signature (the MAP must be signed by both parties before Aug 21).
2) Tranche gating checklist completed and smoke-test results uploaded to the shared Drive for audit.

Recommended commercial posture: offer a conditional 10% onboarding credit for Tranche A only if (a) Redwood fails the acceptance due to a production/runtime defect that we can reproduce in staging within 48 hours, and (b) Acme delivered the test harness and data cleanup by Aug 21. Otherwise, the rolling extension can be used once without commercial credit (to cover customer-side blockages).

Recommended next steps: Vivek, ask Claire to confirm the Aug 19/21 dates in writing and request procurement to accept the redlined SOW we will send. Ben, can you draft a short addendum and redline the SOW with the gating language? Jonas, prepare the Drive folder and one-click evidence checklist so we can send a link with the SOW.

Naomi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Escalation: executive summary and proposed approval (one-week extension + conditional credit)

Team / Claire / Procurement —

Summary of status and ask:
- Risk: Data-cleanup uncertainty could push Acme's Tranche A acceptance by 1–2 business days (Aug 21).
- Proposed quick resolution: offer a one-week rolling extension for Tranche A (no credit) if delay is customer-attributable; offer a conditional 10% onboarding credit if delay is demonstrably Redwood runtime-related and the test harness/data were timely.
- Preconditions: signed MAP (by Aug 21), SOW addendum executed, evidence uploaded to shared Drive.

Commercial impact (estimate): 10% onboarding credit applied to first month = ~$12k (for ACME-2026-789) if triggered. Operational impact: minimal if used as a single rolling extension.

Requesting executive approval to present the SOW addendum and DocuSign link to Acme procurement today. If approved, Naomi will finalize the wording; Ben will attach the redline; Jonas will create the evidence folder and share the link.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.net/sign/abc123-map-extension
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-789

Please reply with APPROVE to route to procurement before EOD PT.

Thanks —
